summary:
THE CENTRAL CLAIM SURVIVES A HARDER TEST THAN THE ONE IT WAS MADE ON, AND I FOUND SIX THINGS THE FIXER DID NOT REPORT, TWO OF THEM FALSE EQUATIONS ITS OWN EDIT PRINTS.

I REBUILT THE MATRIX AT 240 ROWS, NOT 80 (4 CAP_TARGETS x 2 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS x 10 start-cap pairs including the sentinel, negatives, 4095, 4096 and the settling point x 3 CAP_LIFT_MIN), fresh process per cell, BEFORE vs AFTER as described above. 34 rows changed; the transition set is EXACTLY {('FIRED','UNREACHABLE')}; 'gained FIRED: False'; and cap.vocab_arm_honest is identical -- state AND rendered line -- on all 240. So both halves hold: the changed rows really were false FIREDs, and no configuration lost a capability. That result is also STRUCTURALLY FORCED and I say so rather than let the matrix carry more weight than it should: the edit adds `and _lift_moves(c)` to expert_room and `and mask_dead and _lift_moves(c)` to vocab_room, both pure conjuncts, so no predicate can go False->True. The matrix is worth running for the REASON STRINGS and for the neighbours, not for the direction.

EVERY REPRO RE-RUN AND EVERY ONE REPRODUCES VERBATIM. CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=1000 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 was 'Gate cap.valve: FIRED (vocab 1000/ceiling 4096 vs a soft cap in 1..ceiling-1 that the population can reach)' and is now 'UNREACHABLE (vocab 1000/ceiling 4096/one lift -> 1080/mask_dead_rows False ...) -- ... the vocabulary arm has room to earn (1000 against a hard ceiling of 4096) and LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False, so observe refuses every lift it earns by name as dead_rows_unmasked'. CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_FAB_START=12 CAP_LIFT_MIN=0 was FIRED and is now 'UNREACHABLE ... derive.lift_to(12, CAP_LIFT=0.08, CAP_LIFT_MIN=0) = 12'; derive.lift_to(12,0.08,0)=12 and derive.lift_to(12,0.08,8)=20, run by me. THE NEIGHBOURS STILL FIRE: the same vocab corner at LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 -> FIRED ('one lift -> 1080/mask_dead_rows True'); the same expert corner at the shipped CAP_LIFT_MIN=8 -> FIRED ('one lift -> 20'); at CAP_LIFT_MIN=1 -> FIRED ('one lift -> 13'); and CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=500 CAP_VOCAB_START=1000 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 -> FIRED with the vocabulary arm named in the 'ONE ARMED ARM IS STILL DEAD ON ARRIVAL' clause.

THE VACUOUS-CONTROL CLAIM IS TRUE AND I MEASURED IT ON THE BEFORE TREE. All eight corners of CAP_TARGETS x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS at the sentinel caps give cap.valve fired=False reachable=False, every one carrying 'experts 4096/ceiling 4096' or 'vocab 4096/ceiling 4096' -- the sentinel resolves to the hard ceiling and the `cap >= ceiling` arm answers first. A control run entirely inside the unreachable arm cannot detect a change to the fired arm, so D15's control for cap.valve measured nothing. CONFIRMED, and D15's own ruling is untouched by it: cap.vocab_arm_honest is identical on all 240 of my rows.

WHAT I BROKE. THE EDIT PRINTS A FALSE EQUATION ON A REACHABLE CONFIGURATION, which is the thing this spine says is worse than printing nothing. I swept 1320 cells adding CAP_LIFT to the axes and machine-checked each rendered line against its own numbers: 100 cells fail. At CAP_LIFT=-0.5 CAP_FAB_START=12 CAP_LIFT_MIN=0 the new clause prints 'ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT ... = 12, because int(-0.5 x 12) truncates to zero and the floor does not make it up' -- int(-0.5 x 12) is -6, not zero, and it is the FLOOR that saves the cap, the exact opposite of what the sentence says. Worse, at CAP_LIFT=-0.5 CAP_LIFT_MIN=-100 CAP_FAB_START=12 lift_to returns 6: the gate prints 'one lift -> 6' in its arithmetic and 'ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT ... = 6' in its reason, in one line, for a lift that HALVED the cap -- against the module's own founding sentence, 'raised by a little, NEVER LOWERED'. CAP_LIFT is declared U.FRACTION, whose unit string is literally 'fraction 0..1', and NOTHING IN THE TREE ENFORCES THAT RANGE: build() accepts -0.5 without a word. A SECOND FALSE EQUATION IS OLDER BUT THE EDIT IS WHAT MAKES IT VISIBLE AND DID NOT FIX IT: at FAB_SLOTS=10 CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_LIFT_MIN=0 the line reads '(experts 10/ceiling 10/one lift -> 10 ...) -- ... every lift derive.lift_to computes lands above the ceiling and is refused as at_hard_ceiling'. The number the edit added, 'one lift -> 10', refutes the sentence beside it.

AND THE ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE THE ITEM 4 ARGUMENT RESTS ON IS UNSUPPORTED AND POINTS THE WRONG WAY. Both docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3262 and src/capacity/levers.py:171 say 'at least two agents declined to widen a signature partly because they believed the wire alternative was nearly exhausted'. A scarce wire budget is a reason to WIDEN a signature, not to decline to; every documented instance of the miscount pushes AGAINST wires, not against signatures -- Q-EVAL-11 TOOK option (a), widen the signature, and eval/api.py says in its own words the wire 'lost on its merits, not on its price'; the capacity/levers.py sentence warned that adding four couplings 'would fail at build()'; Q-WORLD-6 point 4 warned against spending a line. I grepped src/, docs/ and all of .rework/ for any corroboration of the claim and the only two hits are the fixer's own two copies of it.

EVERYTHING ELSE HOLDS. NOT_WIRES is 7 rows by import and holds neither d_curve_bpb nor d_shift_at; both ARE rows 2 and 4 of docs/04_CONTRACT.md:95-106's 12-row table, whose preamble states the Coupling.compute ground verbatim. new_valve seeds EXACTLY 8 counters keys and the RECORD TYPES line now names all eight. 23 couplings, 19 wires of 25, 4 intra-package, six edges remain. K12 passes and DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS['EVAL.verification_fit'] names verify_mode. The 4095 overshoot reproduces exactly as filed (one lift -> 4422 against a ceiling of 4096, gate FIRED, nothing in the tree saying refuse-or-clamp), and leaving it as an open question rather than guessing was right. ALL THREE of the fixer's unfinished find/replace items have SINCE LANDED in the working tree by their owners -- I verified each by reading the tree, and one of them now makes a row of the fixer's own carrier table false.

K4 CREDIT IS REAL, NOT A FALSE PASS: I ran tests/test_contract.py::stub_reads myself and CAP's harvested lever set is {fab_start, lift, lift_min, pin_windows, stall_band, targets, vocab_start} -- `lift` and `lift_min` ARE harvested despite the parenthetical continuation, because _split_items is depth-aware and then strips from the first '('. By AST, new_valve names exactly the levers and wires its docstring declares, in both directions.

THE FIFTH DEAD-ON-ARRIVAL IS REAL, NEEDED NO WIRE, AND WAS DOCUMENTED BEFORE IT WAS MEASURED. derive.lift_to is `int(cap) + max(int(floor), int(float(frac) * int(cap)))`, which returns the cap unchanged when both terms round to zero; capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers already wrote that case down as the reason lift_min exists. findings.detail:
THE EIGHT-CORNER CONTROL D15 RESTS ON WAS VACUOUS. VERIFIED SPECIFICALLY, ON THE BEFORE TREE, WHICH IS THE ONLY TREE THE CLAIM IS ABOUT. I built all eight corners of CAP_TARGETS x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS at the shipped (sentinel) caps against the BEFORE mirror and read cap.valve on each: fired=False, reachable=False, on all eight. The rendered lines say why, in the gate's own arithmetic: 'experts 4096/ceiling 4096/settles 1844' and 'vocab 4096/ceiling 4096' -- CAP_FAB_START and CAP_VOCAB_START both default to the sentinel 0, _resolve returns the hard ceiling for it, and the `cap >= ceiling` arm answers before any other test can. So the control ran every one of its cells inside the switched-off arm and could not have detected an interaction on the FIRED arm no matter what the change was. That is a property of the control, exactly as claimed, and NOT of D15's ruling.

D15 ITSELF IS UNHARMED AND I CHECKED THAT DIRECTION TOO, because 'the control was vacuous' is not 'the change was wrong'. cap.vocab_arm_honest -- the gate D15 actually repaired -- is IDENTICAL between the two trees on all 240 of my cells, state and rendered line alike, including the 60 cells where it is in the middle state and the 60 where it fires. So the fixer's edit is a strictly non-vacuous 240-row control for D15's gate, which is what D15 was owed and did not get.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE ITEM: the corner needed to make cap.valve reachable at all is a soft cap with HEADROOM, and no cell of a CAP_TARGETS x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS grid supplies one. Any future control for a CAP gate that does not vary a start cap has the same defect.

The correct home is docs/04_CONTRACT.md:93-106, the 12-row 'Candidates examined and refused as wires' table: d_curve_bpb is its row 2 and d_shift_at its row 4, and its preamble at :88-91 states the ground the sentences use in exactly those words -- 'a Coupling.compute receives only frozen Configs and Config freezes when build() returns'.

THE RULING REALLY DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE CITATION, and I checked that rather than accepting it: the ground is a property of Coupling, not of a table, and I confirmed the two tables are genuinely distinct rather than one being a subset -- the section-0 table's OWN rows mark which of its entries are ADDITIONALLY in NOT_WIRES ('already refused in assemble.NOT_WIRES' on the SIG row, 'd_seed is refused by name in NOT_WIRES' on the d_device/d_seed row), which is noise unless membership is partial, and the d_run_steps row calls its ground 'the second NOT_WIRES ground' while itself appearing in NOT_WIRES. So the document supplies the distinction the old sentences erased. Both corrections are dated, quote what they used to say, and enumerate the seven rows, so the substitution cannot be made again by a reader of either file.

I ALSO CHECKED THE SURROUNDING CLAIMS THE SAME EDIT MAKES, since a correction that lands beside a fresh error is the usual shape: curve_probe's signature really is `(ev, *, units_by_domain, logits_fn, step, rng)`; verification_fit's really is `(ev, *, store_copy, verify_mode, rng)`; EVAL is the destination of no Coupling and its harvested WIRES READ set is {'none'}; and the module docstring's 'three stub markers name P5 and five name P6' is exactly right by grep (3 x 'P5 (eval)', 5 x 'P6 (eval)', 8 total, matching the 8 EVAL keys in DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS). O12 is green.

findings.detail:
THE ARITHMETIC IS RIGHT AND THE FIX IS RIGHT; THE ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE OFFERED FOR WHY IT MATTERS IS UNSUPPORTED AND POINTS THE WRONG WAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS DEFERRED AND NOT CONFIRMED.

WHAT HOLDS. tests/test_couplings.py prints '23 coupling(s) resolved against 9 stand-in package(s); 19 wire(s) of 25 budgeted, 4 intra-package' and spine/wire.py::WIRE_BUDGET is 25, so SIX edges remain, not two. The miscount really was counting the 23 declared couplings against the 25-wire budget; the four intra-package couplings book no edge and are exactly the difference. The consequence clause really was false with it: 19 -> 23 is inside 25 and build() does not refuse it. The correction is made IN PLACE (the sentence was present tense, so past-tensing alone would have left it standing) with a dated paragraph below quoting the old wording. The hypothetical is written as a TRANSITION ('19 -> 23 of the 25') rather than as '23 of 25', which is the honest form and is what K13 can distinguish -- K13 passes.

WHAT DOES NOT. The paragraph's stated reason that this is 'NOT A HARMLESS ARITHMETIC SLIP' is: 'at least two agents declined to widen a signature partly because they believed the wire alternative was nearly exhausted'. I can find no support for it anywhere and it is directionally backwards. A budget believed nearly exhausted is a reason to WIDEN a signature and NOT spend a wire; it cannot be a reason to decline to widen one. Every documented case of the miscount biting pushes AWAY from wires: Q-EVAL-11 TOOK option (a), 'Widen the signature -- taken', and src/eval/api.py::<module> says of the wire alternative 'IT LOST ON ITS MERITS, not on its price'; this file's own corrected sentence warned that adding four couplings 'would fail at build() with an over-budget refusal'; docs/04_CONTRACT.md's Q-WORLD-6 point 4 warned against spending 'one of the last lines'. The very next sentence of the fixer's own paragraph says the bias runs 'toward the option nobody has to justify', which is the signature, contradicting the sentence before it. I grepped src/, docs/, tools/ and the whole of .rework/ for corroboration: the only two hits are the fixer's own two copies. Filed in full under unfinished, because it stands in two files and nothing checks prose.

WHAT IS SHORT. src/spine/assemble.py's FAB.manage_every -> WORLD.d_manage_period_windows NOT_WIRES row carries, present tense, 'It would also spend one of the last coupling lines on a WORLD.manage that is itself deferred today' -- the SAME sentence, about the SAME ruling, as the Q-WORLD-6 point 4 the fixer corrected as a carrier. By the table's own criterion it is a carrier, and it is neither in the table nor in unfinished. The fixer's own repro string names the hit ('src/spine/assemble.py:1196's ("one of the last coupling lines")') and then drops it, which is worse than not having looked: the file's rhetoric is REPRODUCED VERBATIM into docs/03_WIRING.md:188 by tools/render_wiring.py, so the un-filed copy propagates into a second file automatically while the filed copy does not.

AND ONE ROW IS NOW FALSE. Row 3 says src/eval/levers.py::<module> is 'still standing'. It is not: its owner has since landed the correction and that file now reads 'so SIX edges remain in the whole tree' plus 'An earlier revision of this sentence said "two more edges"; that was a miscount and it travelled -- do not propagate it.' The fixer could not have known at write time, but the tree today carries a false status row in a file the fixer owns, and no check reads it.

THE REFUTATION IN THE SAME ITEM IS CORRECT AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN WAVING IT THROUGH: docs/proposals/02_ROUTER_RECURSION.md's '(`WIRE_BUDGET` is 25; 19 are spent)' matches the live tree exactly and draws no scarcity conclusion. THE NARROWING IS CORRECT AND IT DID NOT WEAKEN THE DESIGN IT DEFENDS. The old ground for refusing per-flush rather than at startup -- that a startup refusal 'would remove a configuration that runs today' -- did read as though the valve worked at CAP_TARGETS=vocab with LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False. It does not: I confirmed on that exact configuration that cap.valve now prints UNREACHABLE and cap.vocab_arm_honest prints the middle state 'TESTED AND NOT MET', and that no vocabulary lift is possible under either design. So the LIFTING capability is absent either way and is not what separates them, exactly as the correction says.

THE REPLACEMENT GROUND IS STRONGER, NOT WEAKER, AND IT IS THE ONE THE CLOSED SET ACTUALLY BUYS: a startup refusal ends the process and produces no measurement; the per-flush refusal lets the run train, keeps the expert arm alive at targets=both, and puts a COUNT of earned-and-declined lifts in the block-reason histogram, which is a number no other line produces. The owner's stricter option is still explicitly left open. I checked the direction that would have mattered -- that this docstring edit changed no gate reading -- and the 240-row matrix is identical with and without it, since observe raises NotImplementedError and contributes nothing but contract prose.

The passing note about spine/assemble.py's 'would need no flag' being false as written is correct (a valve that refuses ON a condition must READ that condition), and its owner has since landed the full correction in that row.

findings.detail:
THE OVERSHOOT OPEN QUESTION IS REAL, THE NUMBERS ARE EXACT, AND LEAVING IT UNANSWERED WAS THE RIGHT CALL. Reproduced: at CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=4095 CAP_VOCAB_START=4095 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 the gate prints 'FIRED (experts 4095/ceiling 4096/settles 1844/one lift -> 4422, vocab 4095/ceiling 4096/one lift -> 4422/mask_dead_rows True ...)' -- 4095 + max(8, int(0.08*4095)) = 4095 + 327 = 4422, which is 326 above the hard ceiling of 4096, printed beside the ceiling it exceeds.

I SEARCHED FOR AN ANSWER RATHER THAN ACCEPTING THAT THERE IS NONE. spine/derive.py::lift_to's docstring documents truncation and the floor and says nothing about clamping; capacity/api.py::new_valve's comment describes at_hard_ceiling only for the `cap >= ceiling` case; observe's closed set names at_hard_ceiling without defining its predicate; docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section (:515, :523) lists at_hard_ceiling in the closed set and never says what it tests. So the tree really is silent, both readings are open, and they give cap.valve opposite verdicts on this corner. Encoding one would have frozen a P4 behaviour into a Gate on no authority, which is the false-equation failure arriving from the other direction. The recommendation attached to it (decide it in the contract and in observe's DID IT FIRE line together, since the block-reason set is where it becomes observable) is the right shape, and the two-line change it names would land at the `_lift_moves` site the fix has already opened.

unfinished.detail:
I swept 1320 cells (3 targets x 2 masks x 11 start caps x 5 CAP_LIFT x 4 CAP_LIFT_MIN), rendered cap.valve in a fresh process each, and machine-checked every printed 'derive.lift_to(A, CAP_LIFT=F, CAP_LIFT_MIN=M) = B' against its own numbers. 100 cells fail, in two shapes, all of them at CAP_LIFT < 0.

SHAPE 1 -- THE REASON IS FALSE WHILE THE VERDICT IS TRUE. At {'CAP_TARGETS':'experts','CAP_FAB_START':'12','CAP_LIFT':'-0.5','CAP_LIFT_MIN':'0'} the line reads '...ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT: derive.lift_to(12, CAP_LIFT=-0.5, CAP_LIFT_MIN=0) = 12, because int(-0.5 x 12) truncates to zero and the floor does not make it up...'. int(-0.5 x 12) is -6, not zero, and it is the FLOOR (max(0, -6) = 0) that keeps the cap where it is -- the exact opposite of 'the floor does not make it up'. Same at caps 50, 100, 500, 1000, 1844 and at CAP_LIFT=-0.5 with every CAP_LIFT_MIN <= 0.

SHAPE 2 -- THE VERDICT IS FALSE TOO, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE ARITHMETIC ON ITS OWN LINE. At {'CAP_TARGETS':'experts','CAP_FAB_START':'12','CAP_LIFT':'-0.5','CAP_LIFT_MIN':'-100'} the line reads 'UNREACHABLE (experts 12/ceiling 4096/settles 1844/one lift -> 6 ...) -- ... ONE EARNED LIFT DOES NOT MOVE IT: derive.lift_to(12, CAP_LIFT=-0.5, CAP_LIFT_MIN=-100) = 6'. The cap MOVED, from 12 to 6. `_lift_moves` is `derive.lift_to(c, cap.lift, cap.lift_min) > c`, so a cap that goes DOWN fails the test and is reported as one that does not move. Reproduced at caps 12, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 1844, 2000 and 4095, on both arms.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A CORNER. The module's founding sentence is 'may have its ceiling raised, by a little, NEVER LOWERED', and CAP_LIFT=-0.5 produces a lift that lowers it with nothing anywhere refusing the configuration: `lift = Lever(0.08, ..., U.FRACTION)` and spine/units.py:292 defines FRACTION as the STRING 'fraction 0..1' -- a label, not a constraint. `assemble.build(environ={'CAP_LIFT':'-0.5'})` succeeds without a word. So the tree accepts a lever value outside its own declared range, converts it into a cap-lowering mechanism, and the gate that exists to say whether the mechanism can move now says it cannot while printing the number that shows it did.

THE SHAPE OF THE REPAIR IS THE OWNER'S CALL AND I AM NOT GUESSING IT, because the two candidates give different behaviour and one of them is a design decision: (a) refuse CAP_LIFT outside 0..1 (and CAP_LIFT_MIN below 0) at startup, in capacity/api.py::startup_refusals or wherever the owner puts lever-range refusals -- after which `_lift_moves` and its two `dead` clauses are correct as written and no prose changes; or (b) leave the range open and make the clause tell the truth, which means `_lift_moves` distinguishing 'unchanged' from 'lowered' and the reason text branching on `int(cap.lift * c)` being zero versus negative. (a) is the one consistent with 'never lowered' and it is the only one that also closes the invariant. VERIFICATION AFTER EITHER LANDS: re-run the sweep driver (/tmp/.../scratchpad/v/sweep.py, which is outside the repo and takes a tree root as its argument) and it should print 'problems 0'; the 240-row matrix must be unchanged for all CAP_LIFT=0.08 cells, and the four in-range neighbours in my finding 0 must still print FIRED with 'one lift -> 20', '-> 13', '-> 1080' and '-> 540'.

src/capacity/levers.py:171 and docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3262-3263 both say: 'at least two agents declined to widen a signature partly because they believed the wire alternative was nearly exhausted.'

(a) IT IS UNSUPPORTED. `grep -rn 'declined to widen|nearly exhausted|wire alternative' src/ docs/ .rework/` returns exactly these two lines and nothing else -- no audit record, no ruling, no docstring anywhere in the tree says any agent took that decision on that number.

(b) IT IS BACKWARDS. A wire budget believed nearly exhausted is a reason to widen a signature and NOT spend a wire. It cannot be a reason to DECLINE to widen one. Every documented case of this miscount biting runs the other way: docs/04_CONTRACT.md's Q-EVAL-11 records option '(a) Widen the signature -- taken'; src/eval/api.py::<module> says of the wire alternative 'IT LOST ON ITS MERITS, not on its price'; src/capacity/levers.py's own corrected sentence warned that adding four couplings 'would fail at build() with an over-budget refusal'; docs/04_CONTRACT.md's Q-WORLD-6 point 4 warned against spending 'one of the last lines'. All four push AGAINST wires.

(c) IT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN NEXT SENTENCE. The doc continues: the wrong number 'biases every design choice that weighs a wire against an argument, and it does so in the direction of the choice nobody has to justify'. The choice nobody has to justify is the widened signature -- i.e. the bias is TOWARD widening, which is the opposite of 'declined to widen'.

THE UNDERLYING POINT IS SOUND AND SHOULD SURVIVE: a budget number wrong in the scarce direction does silently bias design choices, and correcting it is not bookkeeping. What has to change is the direction and the evidence. SUGGESTED FORM, using only what the tree can support: 'A budget number wrong in the SCARCE direction biases every choice that weighs a wire against a widened signature, and it biases it toward the signature -- the option nobody has to justify at build(). The tree records the bias in the sentences themselves rather than in any agent's stated motive: this file told a porter that four couplings that already exist would be refused at build(); Q-WORLD-6 point 4 called a legal row "one of the last lines"; and src/eval/levers.py told a reader that only two edges were left in the whole tree.'
